q3Options.text: Because magnitude reflects the vector's length, not how semantically related the underlying texts are
Because dot product is too slow to compute for large vectors
q3Options.reason: That's not the reason, dot product is actually a component of cosine similarity itself, and isn't meaningfully slower. The issue is what raw dot product means, not how fast it runs.

q3Options.text: Because raw dot product can never be negative
q3Options.reason: Raw dot product can absolutely be negative, for vectors pointing in opposing directions. That's not the reason magnitude gets divided out.

q4Options.text: Its 5 best-scoring documents anyway, even though none of them are actually relevant
An empty result set automatically, since nothing matches well
q4Options.reason: Not automatically, top-k without a threshold has no concept of 'not good enough,' it always returns exactly k results (or fewer if the collection has less than k documents), ranked by whatever scored highest, relevant or not.

q4Options.text: An error, since no document scores above a reasonable relevance level
q4Options.reason: No error, similarity scoring doesn't know what 'reasonable' means without an explicit threshold, it just returns the mathematically highest-scoring k documents.
